PAPERS.short: Park residential testbed low-cost indoor particle sensor ML vs linear calibration data volume source heterogeneity 2026
PAPERS.title: Data-Dependent Performance of Machine Learning Calibration for Low-Cost Indoor Particle Sensors.
PAPERS.pm: Indoor PM from low-cost optical particle sensors against reference instruments, three controlled source conditions
PAPERS.endpoint: Calibration R2, normalised error and bias under intra-, cross- and multi-source training
PAPERS.affil: Dankook University, South Korea; Sejong University, South Korea
PAPERS.n: Full-scale residential testbed, three particle-source conditions, linear regression against three ML models under intra-source, cross-source and multi-source training. Adding sensor particle-number channels raised R2 by 0.05-0.10 and cut normalised error by up to 25%. LightGBM was the best nonlinear model and gained most from more training data, but at fixed data volume greater source heterogeneity lowered its error and bias without raising R2 or beating linear regression; with more multi-source data it won on error and bias while linear regression kept the higher R2. The abstract names neither the sensor models nor the reference, and three sources in one house is a narrow test of transfer. Relevance: direct - 'ML beats linear' is metric- and data-dependent, so calibration claims must state both.

PAPERS.short: Ramadan review spatial uncertainty indoor air quality monitoring mobile sensing position error response-time displacement 2026
PAPERS.title: Spatial Intelligence for Indoor Air Quality: Integrating Spatial Uncertainty Into Monitoring, Exposure Assessment, and Ventilation Control
PAPERS.pm: Indoor pollutant concentrations from fixed and mobile sensors; position and response-time uncertainty
PAPERS.endpoint: Propagation of spatial uncertainty through monitoring, exposure and control chains
PAPERS.affil: Istanbul Aydin University, Turkiye; Abu Dhabi University, UAE
PAPERS.n: Scored review of 91 indoor air-quality publications using a 'Building Spatial Intelligence' framework: capability profile, a propagation level for how far spatial uncertainty travels downstream, and nine system archetypes. None of the 91 attaches a quantified uncertainty to measurement position, none quantifies sensor-response displacement, and none of the 31 mobile-platform studies reports position uncertainty. The key physical point: on a moving platform, speed times sensor time constant typically displaces a reading further than positioning error, a systematic shift correctable by re-registration. The scoring is the authors' own construct and the corpus is not claimed to represent the field. Relevance: direct - mobile low-cost PM mapping inherits exactly this lag-displacement error, and the scoring dataset is released.

PAPERS.short: Bengaluru CAAQM hybrid gap-filling random forest proxy station PM2.5 PM10 trends 2016-2025
PAPERS.title: Hybrid gap-filling framework and spatiotemporal analysis of urban air pollution in Bengaluru, India.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5, PM10, NOx, NH3, O3 from three continuous regulatory monitors, gaps filled by interpolation, random forest and proxy stations
PAPERS.endpoint: Data completeness; trends and exceedance days 2016-2025
PAPERS.affil: K S School of Engineering and Management, India; K S School of Engineering and Management, India
PAPERS.n: Three Bengaluru CAAQM stations (Peenya, Majestic, Bellandur), 2016-2025. Short gaps are linearly interpolated, longer ones filled by random forest regression and proxy-station substitution, then trends, seasonality and exceedances computed on the reconstructed series. PM2.5 declined at Peenya while PM10 rose at Peenya and Bellandur, read as road dust and construction; exceedance days cluster in winter and pre-monsoon and are far more frequent against WHO than Indian NAAQS limits. The abstract reports no gap-filling validation metrics or the fraction of each series imputed, so trends could partly be imputation artefacts. Relevance: indirect - gap-filled regulatory series are the usual reference for sensor calibration in Indian cities, and imputed reference values must be flagged before use.

PAPERS.short: Clemente western Mediterranean suburban rural PM2.5 oxidative potential DTT AA PMF biomass burning traffic 2026
PAPERS.title: What drives the oxidative potential of fine particles? Insights from suburban and rural sites of the western Mediterranean.
PAPERS.design: Intensive field campaign, PMF source apportionment
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 filters; OP by DTT and ascorbic-acid acellular assays; PMF with GLS regression
PAPERS.endpoint: Source contributions to volume-normalised OP-DTT and OP-AA
PAPERS.affil: Miguel Hernandez University, Spain; Miguel Hernandez University, Spain
PAPERS.n: PM2.5 filters at one suburban and one rural site in south-eastern Spain, OP by DTT and AA assays, PMF sources regressed on OP by GLS. Mass and volume-normalised OP were higher at the suburban site. In winter biomass burning was nearly 50% of rural PM2.5 mass and the dominant driver of both OP measures there; at the suburban site traffic and biomass burning drove OP. In summer aged sea salt and secondary sulfate contributed substantially, which the authors attribute to co-varying redox-active organics or acid-enhanced metal solubility rather than sulfate itself. Two sites, source-OP regression without uncertainty in the abstract, and no exposure or health link. Relevance: indirect - mass-only sensors miss the source-dependent toxicity this shows; OP varies by season at fixed mass.

PAPERS.short: Yadate global wildfire smoke PM2.5 PM10 O3 mortality systematic review meta-analysis WHO region 2026
PAPERS.title: Mortality risk associated with wildfire smoke exposure across global, regional, and country levels: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
PAPERS.pm: Wildfire-attributed PM2.5, PM10 and O3 as modelled or apportioned in the included studies
PAPERS.endpoint: All-cause, cardiovascular, respiratory and cancer mortality
PAPERS.affil: Australian National University, Australia; Australian National University, Australia
PAPERS.n: 32 studies (>394 million deaths), 25 meta-analysed, random effects, PROSPERO-registered, Navigation Guide grading. Per 10 ug/m3 wildfire PM2.5: all-cause mortality RR 1.066 (1.014-1.121), cardiovascular 1.020 (1.010-1.030); respiratory 1.112 (0.953-1.298) and cancer 1.066 (0.954-1.192) were imprecise. By WHO region the largest all-cause estimate was Europe (1.045, 1.024-1.066). The pooled all-cause RR exceeds the largest regional all-cause estimate given, which points to strong between-study heterogeneity the abstract does not report, and the smoke-attribution methods (chemical transport, satellite, statistical) differ across studies. Relevance: indirect - smoke-specific PM2.5 is a modelled quantity; dense sensor networks are the obvious route to measured smoke exposure for these cohorts.

PAPERS.short: Navaratnam 136 LMIC health impact assessment WHO IT3 AQG PM2.5 NO2 mortality VSL cost-of-illness 2026
PAPERS.title: Health and economic impacts of achieving WHO air quality targets in 136 Low- and Middle-Income countries.
PAPERS.pm: High-resolution global PM2.5 and NO2 surfaces at ~1 km with gridded population
PAPERS.endpoint: Avoided mortality and incidence; VSL and cost-of-illness valuation
PAPERS.affil: University of Cambridge, UK; University of Cambridge, UK
PAPERS.n: Health impact assessment across 136 LMICs at ~1 km with GBD 2021 baseline rates and published concentration-response functions. Meeting the PM2.5 Interim Target 3 (15 ug/m3) would cut annual mortality 16.04% (6.58 million, UI 4.7-8.3 million); the 5 ug/m3 guideline 22.97% (9.43 million, 6.8-11.7 million), valued at Int$5.5 and 8.4 trillion, 7.0% and 10.7% of aggregate LMIC GDP. NO2 targets add 1.06-2.79%. The intervals carry concentration-response uncertainty only, as the authors state, so exposure-surface error in data-sparse LMICs is not propagated. Relevance: indirect - in LMICs the gridded PM2.5 input is least constrained by ground monitors, which is where sensor networks change the answer.

PAPERS.short: Park children atopic dermatitis ambient air pollution systematic review meta-analysis GRADE PM2.5 PM10 NO2 2026
PAPERS.title: Air Pollution and Atopic Dermatitis in Children: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
PAPERS.pm: Ambient NO2, SO2, PM10, PM2.5, O3, CO and traffic pollution as assessed in the included studies
PAPERS.endpoint: Atopic dermatitis prevalence, incidence, severity and outpatient visits
PAPERS.affil: University of Toronto, Canada; Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre, Canada
PAPERS.n: 52 observational studies of children (<18 y), random effects, ROBINS-E and GRADE. Per 10 ug/m3, PM2.5 OR 1.04 (1.00-1.08) and PM10 OR 1.19 (1.06-1.35) for atopic dermatitis prevalence, both moderate certainty; outpatient visits rose with NO2 (OR 3.46, 1.06-11.31) and SO2 (3.96, 1.00-15.65). Incidence and severity findings were mixed or null. The gas ORs for visits are implausibly large per 10 ug/m3 with very wide CIs, suggesting few, heterogeneous time-series studies; prevalence associations are mostly cross-sectional and cannot order exposure and onset. Relevance: indirect - the PM10 > PM2.5 gradient for a skin endpoint hints at the coarse fraction, which low-cost optical sensors measure least well.

PAPERS.short: Verma Kawasaki disease ambient air pollution systematic review meta-analysis null PM2.5 2026
PAPERS.title: Ambient Air Pollution and Kawasaki Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Epidemiological Evidence.
PAPERS.pm: Ambient PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, O3, CO standardised to 10 ug/m3
PAPERS.affil: Rama Medical College Hospital, India; Makerere University, Uganda
PAPERS.n: 13 observational studies, mostly Asian, random effects with HR and OR pooled as RR per 10 ug/m3. PM2.5 RR 1.00 (0.985-1.016, I2 43.8%, Egger p=0.27); PM10 1.00 (0.983-1.022); SO2 1.008 (0.966-1.051); NO2 0.99 (0.989-1.009); O3 and CO 1.013 (0.981-1.046). No pollutant was associated with Kawasaki disease. Mixing case-crossover, time-series and cohort designs with different lags into one pooled estimate can cancel real short-window associations, which the authors acknowledge; the search closed December 2024. A null result with tight CIs around 1.00 is still informative. Relevance: indirect - a well-bounded null that counts against Kawasaki disease as a PM-triggered endpoint.

PAPERS.short: Kanchanasuta Bangkok AQHI temporal transportability PM2.5 AQI coarse PM cardiovascular morbidity 2021-2024
PAPERS.title: Temporal Transportability and Component Deconstruction of a Multipollutant Air Quality Health Index: Health Information Beyond the Composite Score.
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5, PMcoarse (PM10-PM2.5), O3, SO2 and composite AQHI / PM2.5-based AQI from Bangkok monitors
PAPERS.endpoint: Daily total, cardiovascular and respiratory hospital morbidity
PAPERS.affil: Mahidol University, Thailand; Bangkok Metropolitan Administration, Thailand
PAPERS.n: Out-of-period test of the Bangkok AQHI, 2021-2024: 1,461 days, 26 postcodes, 23 hospitals, negative binomial models against a PM2.5-based AQI. The composite AQHI did not consistently improve fit or out-of-time prediction over the AQI. PMcoarse (PM10 minus PM2.5) stayed associated with cardiovascular morbidity after nonlinear PM2.5 and gas adjustment, MA0-1 IRR 1.175 (1.076-1.283); the increment is not given in the abstract. On discordant days, removing O3 brought every AQHI below 7. Multiple comparisons are acknowledged and several signals are not multiplicity-robust. Relevance: direct - coarse PM carries independent cardiovascular signal, and a PM2.5-only sensor network cannot report it.

PAPERS.short: Xi 1898 Chinese counties green blue space life expectancy mediation PM1 PM1-2.5 PM2.5-10 2000-2021
PAPERS.title: Associations of green and blue spaces with life expectancy are partly explained by lower ambient particulate matter: Evidence from 1898 Chinese counties over two decades.
PAPERS.pm: County PM1, PM1-2.5 and PM2.5-10 from high-resolution gridded datasets
PAPERS.affil: Sun Yat-sen University, China; Sun Yat-sen University, China
PAPERS.n: 1,898 counties, 2000-2021, generalised additive mixed models in a mediation framework. A simultaneous 10-percentage-point rise in green and blue cover was associated with 0.968 years more life expectancy (0.945-0.991); lower PM explained about 23%, PM1 most (0.109 y, 0.095-0.123), then PM2.5-10 (0.065 y) and PM1-2.5 (0.050 y). Indirect effects were strongest in the Northwest and roughly twice as large in underdeveloped regions. County-level ecological mediation with modelled, collinear size fractions cannot separate deposition by vegetation from the fact that greener counties are less industrial. Relevance: indirect - size-fractionated PM1 surfaces are uncommon; PM1 channels on optical sensors could test them.

PAPERS.short: Kim GBD 2023 Asia Alzheimer dementia mortality attributable air pollution tobacco FPG BMI decomposition 1990-2023
PAPERS.title: Decoding the Drivers of Alzheimer's Disease and Other Dementias Mortality in Asia, 1990-2023: A Global Burden of Diseases Study 2023.
PAPERS.pm: GBD 2023 air-pollution risk factor (ambient PM, household air pollution) as modelled by GBD
PAPERS.endpoint: ADOD mortality attributable to risk factors, adults >=70 y
PAPERS.affil: Kyung Hee University, South Korea; Kyung Hee University, South Korea
PAPERS.n: GBD 2023 comparative risk assessment in 34 Asian countries, adults aged 70 and over, with Das Gupta decomposition into population growth, ageing and epidemiological change. ADOD mortality was highest in high-income Asia Pacific (661 per 100,000, UI 190-1,505) and lowest in Central Asia (273). The abstract calls air pollution 'a major driver' but gives no attributable rate for it, while high fasting glucose rose everywhere (high-income Asia Pacific 76 to 139 per 100,000). The uncertainty intervals span roughly an order of magnitude, and the air-pollution-dementia link enters as a GBD relative-risk function, not an estimate from these data. Relevance: indirect - burden accounting only.

PAPERS.short: Duan KDM4B PTX3 dendritic cell senescence severe asthma HDM PM2.5 mouse model biologic non-response 2026
PAPERS.title: KDM4B-PTX3-mediated dendritic cell senescence drives severe asthma and predicts biologic non-response.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 used as one airway trigger in mouse models alongside house dust mite; dose not stated in the abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: cDC2 senescence, airway remodelling, plasma PTX3, biologic response
PAPERS.affil: Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine, China; Shenzhen University, China
PAPERS.n: Discovery cohort of 226 patients plus scRNA-seq, ChIP/ATAC-seq and HDM and PM2.5 mouse models. Plasma PTX3 was raised in severe asthma and tracked impaired lung function and exacerbations; CD1c+ cDC2 cells were its main source, and DC-specific Ptx3 knockout showed lung cDC2 supply about 61% of circulating PTX3. KDM4B demethylates H3K9me3 at PTX3 and PTX3 induces KDM4B through NF-kB, a loop the authors call conserved across triggers; inhaled KDM4B inhibition was tested. PM2.5 is one of two triggers and its dose and source are not given, so the PM-specific contribution cannot be separated from HDM. Relevance: indirect - mechanism for PM-triggered severe asthma, not an exposure result.

PAPERS.short: Ebtini PHOTO-LAC Siberian biomass burning flaming smouldering ageing PAH oxy-PAH resin diterpenoids TOCA-PIMS 2026
PAPERS.title: Compositional changes of biomass burning aerosols during ageing in the Photochemical Large Aerosol Chamber (PHOTO-LAC).
PAPERS.pm: Biomass-burning PM from flaming and smouldering Siberian fuels; OC, EC, PAH, oxy-PAH and resin acids
PAPERS.endpoint: Emission factors and composition change under alternating photochemical and dark ageing
PAPERS.affil: University of Rostock, Germany; University of Rostock, Germany
PAPERS.n: Siberian biomass emissions aged in a large chamber under alternating light and dark at dense-plume concentrations. Smouldering emitted more OC (27 vs 2.8 g/kg) and far more PAH (430 vs 21 mg/kg) and oxy-PAH (230 vs 17 mg/kg) but less EC (7.8 vs 21 g/kg) than flaming. Flaming plumes formed secondary OC on ageing, smouldering lost OC; PAHs and oxy-PAHs fell mainly in the first photochemical step and then held. Resin diterpenoids were large in smouldering emissions and abietic acid by TOCA-PIMS is proposed as a fresh-smoke marker. Single fuel region and chamber wall losses are not addressed in the abstract. Relevance: indirect - smoke toxicity per unit mass shifts with combustion phase and age, which mass sensors do not see.

PAPERS.short: Li Jinan five tree species foliar PM2.5 PM10 accumulation O3 deposition isoprene AMItree screening 2026
PAPERS.title: Balancing the Dual Roles of Urban Vegetation in Air Quality Regulation: An Organismal-Scale Screening Framework of Pollutant Deposition and Biogenic Emissions Across Five Temperate Tree Species
PAPERS.pm: Tree-level net foliar PM2.5 and PM10 accumulation by foliar elution; O3 deposition by gradient method; isoprene by branch enclosure
PAPERS.endpoint: Per-tree PM accumulation, O3 deposition, isoprene emission; composite AMItree score
PAPERS.affil: QingDao iESLab Electronic Co., China; Shandong Normal University, China
PAPERS.n: Five temperate species in Jinan, field-measured and upscaled to the canopy. Platycladus orientalis had the highest net foliar accumulation, 1.22 g/day per tree for PM2.5 and 3.02 for PM10; Platanus acerifolia had the highest O3 deposition (0.60 m3/s per tree, 4.5 times the lowest) but emitted 220 mg C/h isoprene, while Styphnolobium japonicum emitted 596 and scored near zero on the composite index (0.02-0.04). Foliar elution measures retained mass, not net removal from breathing-height air, and the index weights are partly expert-chosen. Relevance: indirect - species-level PM deposition rates for urban-greening claims, not an exposure measurement.

PAPERS.short: Mirkhanian coastal California wildfire marine boundary layer satellite AOD surface PM2.5 coupling 2026
PAPERS.title: Marine boundary layer influence on satellite AOD and surface PM2.5 during coastal California wildfires
PAPERS.pm: Satellite aerosol optical depth and surface PM2.5
PAPERS.affil: University of California, Irvine, USA; University of California, Irvine, USA
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: Crossref carries a one-sentence graphical-abstract line and no abstract; Semantic Scholar had nothing further at issue time. The deposited line states that satellite AOD-PM2.5 coupling can vary with boundary-layer structure and transport regime during coastal wildfires; no data, method, sites or effect sizes are available, so no finding is asserted here. Both authors are at UC Irvine public health. Relevance: direct if borne out - when marine-layer capping decouples column AOD from surface PM2.5, satellite-fused smoke surfaces fail exactly where coastal populations live, and ground sensors become the only constraint. Recheck at the W46 abstract sweep.

PAPERS.short: Singh Sathish Banerjee size-resolved fine aerosol composition optics alveolar dose two contrasting environments 2026
PAPERS.title: Size resolves what bulk mass misses: composition, optics and alveolar dose of fine aerosol over two contrasting environments
PAPERS.pm: Size-resolved fine aerosol; composition, optics and alveolar dose
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: Elsevier day-0 deposit with no abstract in Crossref or Semantic Scholar at issue time; no finding is asserted. Title and author list (Singh, Sathish, Anand, Chakraborty ... Banerjee) match the IIT Kanpur group whose paired Kanpur-Mumbai size-resolved study (Environ Res, 10.1016/j.envres.2026.126094) ran in the 5 November issue; this is a separate DOI in a different journal, so it is carried and the overlap in data will be checked when the abstract appears. Geography is inferred from that companion paper. Relevance: direct in theme - alveolar dose by size fraction is the quantity bulk optical PM2.5 sensors approximate worst.

PAPERS.short: Lee Al-Kindi visceral adiposity susceptibility air pollution cardiovascular commentary 2026
PAPERS.title: Beyond exposure: Visceral adiposity and susceptibility to air pollution.
PAPERS.affil: SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry, USA; Houston Methodist, USA
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: PubMed record without an abstract in the American Journal of Preventive Cardiology; no finding is asserted. The title frames visceral adiposity as a susceptibility modifier of air-pollution cardiovascular effects, a thread consistent with the BMI- and diabetes-stratified results carried in the 6 November issue. The authors sit in environmental science (SUNY ESF) and preventive cardiology (Houston Methodist). Without text there is no claim to assess. Relevance: indirect - effect modification by body composition matters for interpreting personal-monitor exposure-response in cohorts with imaging-derived fat measures.
